summary: Newberry County tower whose record lists the owner as National Forest and marks it removed; OpenStreetMap still has a tower entry at the spot.

facts.agency: National Forest (agency not named in the source)
facts.status_note: Listed as removed. The OpenStreetMap entry still carries the name at the spot, but no source says whether a tower stands there.

evidence.supports: Map name: Long Lane Lookout Tower
The state agency ended its tower network in 1993 along with several other state and federal agencies
evidence.quote: In 1993, the South Carolina Forestry Commission officially ended its tower network, along with several other state and federal government agencies.

evidence.supports: Network obsolete given aircraft, satellites and cellular phones
evidence.quote: The tower network was obsolete given the availability of aircraft, satellites, and cellular phones to report forest fires.

evidence.supports: Decommissioned fire towers available for auction since 2003
evidence.quote: fire towers have been decommissioned and available for auction since 2003.

notes_for_editor: Identity: the Forest Lookouts record (Long Lane Branch, Newberry County, National Forest, Removed) and the OpenStreetMap node (Long Lane Lookout Tower, same county, same coordinates as the brief) are treated as one structure. No source states that link outright, so the story says it appears to be the same site. The record answers the brief's unknown status with Removed, but gives no date. The brief lacks county and agency fields. Mapcarta gives 479 ft (146 m) for the same point, while the OSM elevation tag is 147 m. The OSM node was last edited about two years ago and its tags do not show whether a tower stands. No build date, height or staffing found.
